smells.finding: decide_session_start is now ~105 lines (spine_rail.py:1697-1803) and does four separable things in one body: select an entry the acting agent owns, fall through to the blind scan, WRITE a bind-on-resume entry via a nested _resume_mutate closure, and render the resume context. The rework added ~45 lines to it, all comment. This is not a style note on this gate: the selection branch and the bind branch interact -- withholding at the first is what routes a session into the second -- and that interaction is blocker B4. Nothing in the function makes the two branches look connected, and at this length nothing invites the reader to check. Extracting the bind-on-resume step would put the coupling on one line of the caller, where the missing discriminator ('no binding at all' vs 'visible bindings I own none of') would be visible. The first reviewer flagged long-method here too, and its extraction WAS the B2 fix; the same smell in the same function now points at the fix's own defect.

The rework REMOVED the one real instance: the ownership filter, previously inline at decide_stop and missing at decide_session_start, is now the single _own_entries. The apparent leftover -- decide_stop re-evaluating _is_own_entry(owners.get(spine_path), own_key) at :1643 after _own_entries already computed it -- is not redundant: when `own` is empty and the fallback takes mid_flight[0], the re-check can still be True for an unattributable entry (owner_key None reads as OWN). Replacing it with `if own:` would change behaviour. Checked, not assumed.

(owners, own_key) travel together at both call sites and into _own_entries, and both sites compose them the same way (session_view_provenance(binding, sid) + binding_key(data)). Three values that always appear together and jointly mean 'the ownership question for this payload' are a textbook clump; a small resolver returning the pair would name it once.

override.reason: The handoff's latitude was what replaces the skip at each call site, not a data model for ownership. Introducing a parameter object on top would be abstraction the handoff did not ask for and that no third caller justifies.

override.repo_standard: The hook ships as ONE stdlib-only file installed at a fixed path; the suite pins the import block byte-for-byte and forbids cross-module imports.
override.reason: Cohesion here cannot be bought by splitting modules, because the file's single-file-ness is the enforced constraint, not an accident. The available remedy is intra-file extraction, which I have flagged under long-method where it actually bites. Flagging divergent-change on top would be recommending a module split the standard forbids.

smells.finding: _own_entries is documented for 'any sequence whose element [0] is the abs spine path', which reads generic for two known callers -- but two callers is a real seam rather than a hypothetical one (global-everyone.md, Deep-module vocabulary), and naming the comparison once is precisely what stops the two sites drifting. Not speculative.

The rework added roughly 45 comment lines to decide_session_start and grew the module section header from 4 lines to 19, and the comments argue a design property the code does not have. Four of those sentences are false (recorded on w5), and the two that matter -- 'Nothing another agent claimed is ever substituted: this site withholds rather than guessing' and the header's 'the blind scan below ... is not this rule's business' -- are exactly the reassurance a reader would rely on to conclude blocker B4 cannot happen. This is the smell in its harmful form: prose standing in for a structural guarantee, in a function long enough that no reader can cheaply check it. Fowler's remedy applies literally here -- when the comment explains how two branches of a long function interact, extract the branches so the interaction is a call. Note the honest counterexample in the same diff: the sentences that keep the qualifier 'from the binding' are all true, so the author could state the narrow claim correctly and only went wrong when generalising it.
